subject: Post-demo: unit-costs with session-warmth & hit-rate assumptions
body:
--- Message 1 (original) ---
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramos <elena@novacorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: unit-costs with session-warmth & hit-rate assumptions

Hi Elena — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick follow-up capturing the pricing & cache assumptions we discussed so your team (and procurement) can evaluate. Summary and asks below.

1) What we demoed
- Redwood hosted inference: predictable latency with session-warmth (session-level KV/prefix caching) and optional prefetch layer.
- Demonstrated a 200ms p50 for the 16k context model with warm sessions.

2) Pricing signals for your finance & procurement teams
- Baseline model unit price (example): $28 / 1M tokens (list, before caching)
- Goal you mentioned: target ~ $9–12 / 1M effective tokens for customer-visible spend (after caching savings)

3) Caching assumptions we used during the demo (please confirm):
- Session-warmth (prefix + KV): initial warm hit for template-heavy prompts, expected to reduce token counts for common prefixes.
- Working assumption: 50% prefix/session hit for the typical flows you described, higher for chat assistants with stable prompts.

4) Ask from NovaCorp (please confirm by EOD Wednesday)
- Typical daily active sessions (DAU) and average tokens/session (both input+output). If you can share ranges (low/mid/high) that’s perfect.
- Any SLAs/latency constraints that would change routing (e.g., must stay on-prem for PII calls).

Next steps
- I’ll loop in Ben (SE) and Monica (CS) to build 3 unit-cost scenarios for your procurement: conservative (30% hit), expected (55% hit), optimistic (80% hit).
- If you can share the usage ranges in the attached spreadsheet, I’ll convert to effective $/1M tokens and run projected monthly spend.

Attachments: NovaCorp_demo_deck_v3.pdf, NovaCorp_estimated_usage.xlsx (please fill the yellow cells)

Thanks — talk soon,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
dylan@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

--- Message 2 (external reply) ---
From: Elena Ramos <elena@novacorp.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novacorp.com
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: unit-costs with session-warmth & hit-rate assumptions

Thanks, Dylan — good recap. A few notes from our side: we completed the usage workbook and attached (see returned file). High-level ranges:
- DAU: 4k / 12k / 35k (low / mid / high)
- Avg tokens/session: 900 / 1,600 / 2,800 (low / mid / high)
- Important: roughly 40% of sessions are guided templates (very similar prompts across sessions); the rest are more ad-hoc.

Procurement asked for two pricing targets: 1) a conservative model the CFO can sign off on for year 1, 2) a stretch target if we hit adoption milestones. The finance team’s quick target is $10 / 1M effective tokens for the conservative plan.

Let us know if the workbook you sent back has everything you need. If helpful, we can schedule a quick 30-min cost-run review on Friday.

- Elena

--- Message 3 (internal: AE -> SE + CS) ---
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: unit-costs with session-warmth & hit-rate assumptions

Ben / Monica — forwarding Elena’s reply + filled workbook. Procurement wants a conservative price target $10/1M effective; they reported a 40% templated session rate. Can you run quick scenario numbers and push back if the $10 target is unrealistic under their mid usage? Specific asks: 
- Build three effective $/1M calculations using our baseline $28/1M (model cost) and the following hit rates: 30%, 55%, 80%. Show the math and monthly spend for the mid usage bucket (12k DAU, 1,600 tokens/session).
- Include an alternative where prefix caching only (no session KV) gives a 25% hit — label it separately.
- If possible, include a suggested packaging: e.g., reserved throughput band or dedicated pool that helps meet their p50 SLO for high-concurrency peaks.

I’ll set up the Friday 30-min review if you think we should walk them through the calc.

Thanks,
D

--- Message 4 (internal reply from Ben SE) ---
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Aug 2027 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo: unit-costs with session-warmth & hit-rate assumptions

Following up with the quick math (rounded). Baseline assumptions: model list = $28 / 1M tokens; "effective tokens" = billed tokens after cache hits removed.

Scenarios (mid bucket = 12,000 DAU, 1,600 tokens/session)
- Sessions/day tokens (unadjusted): 12,000 * 1,600 = 19,200,000 tokens/day (~19.2M)
- Monthly tokens (30d): ~576M tokens/month (unadjusted)

Hit-rate scenarios (effective tokens and $/1M):
1) Prefix-only hit 25% -> effective tokens = 0.75 * 576M = 432M -> effective $/1M = $28 * (432/576) = $21.00 / 1M
2) Conservative session-warmth 30% -> effective tokens = 0.70 * 576M = 403.2M -> effective $/1M ≈ $19.60 / 1M
3) Expected 55% -> effective tokens = 0.45 * 576M = 259.2M -> effective $/1M ≈ $12.60 / 1M
4) Optimistic 80% -> effective tokens = 0.20 * 576M = 115.2M -> effective $/1M ≈ $5.60 / 1M

Monthly cost (approx):
- Prefix-only (25%): 432M * $28 / 1M = $12,096
- Conservative (30%): 403.2M * $28 / 1M = $11,289.6
- Expected (55%): 259.2M * $28 / 1M = $7,257.6
- Optimistic (80%): 115.2M * $28 / 1M = $3,225.6

Notes / recommended packaging:
- The conservative $10/1M target they asked for is below our 'expected' 55% scenario break-even (we show ~ $12.60 / 1M). To get to $10 / 1M with baseline $28 list, they'd need ~64% effective hit rate (0.36 effective), or we’d need a discounted committed price (e.g., list -> $24/1M with 55% hit).
- For procurement ease, propose a Reserved Band with a 12-month commit (reduces list by ~15%) + session-warmth configuration to target 60–65% effective hit; that gets them closer to $10/1M effective.

Action items:
- Dylan: propose Friday 30-min cost-run review (I can present calc + quick slide).
- Monica: can you confirm any non-negotiable SLOs and whether on-prem routing will change packaging?

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
